_what_this_is: The exact Snap/Bitmoji renderer recipe for Crid, the character in the desk overlay. Use it to render more poses and weight stages of the SAME avatar. It is not a license to design a new character. This file previously held a sampled recipe that rendered a DIFFERENT man (solid handlebar moustache, no earrings, face_proportion=13) — that was wrong and has been replaced by the recipe the shipped ladder is actually built from, which lives verbatim in scripts/build-body-ladder.py (RECIPE).
_also_works: Swap /preview/body for /preview/bust for a head-and-shoulders crop, or /preview/head for the face alone.
_derivation: The face parameters are the RECIPE constant in scripts/build-body-ladder.py — recovered from the owner's original avatar URL, plus the two gold hoop earrings. They reproduce the owner's Bitmoji. If the owner ever supplies his Bitmoji avatar id, that id is more authoritative than these numbers — prefer it, and update this file.
_rules: NO CLOTHES — the owner's direction is 'wearing nothing'. He renders as Snap's base body: no camo cargos, no tee, no backpack straps, no shoes. Omit the outfit parameter entirely (outfit=-1 is rejected with HTTP 400). The backpack is a separate prop drawn by the overlay, never part of the render.
rotation MUST be 0. Crid is drawn front-facing. rotation=7 (three-quarter) is what made earlier weight stages look like different people.

body: Snap's renderer only produces seven distinct builds at rotation 0 — 3, 0, 4, 5, 1, 11, 2 (leanest -> heaviest). Every other value (4/6/7/8/9/10/12) returns the same picture as body=4, and 00/000 clamp to body=0. The ladder ships all seven; do not invent stage numbers the renderer does not produce.

Height and head size are fixed across stages — measured, not assumed: every shipped frame has identical ink height and head top (see public/desk-assets/crid/ladder.json). Only width and mass may change.
Render at scale=3 (1050x1400), then let scripts/build-body-ladder.py frame it: ink bottom on y=1325, body axis on x=560.
Never pass these parameters to an image-generation model. They belong to Snap's renderer and nowhere else.
Tone values must be sent as DECIMAL integers. Hex strings in a URL make the renderer answer HTTP 400 with an empty body.

body_stages.2: heaviest (belly, thicker limbs — same measured height and head as every other stage)

current_shipped_renders: public/desk-assets/crid/body-3-r0.webp (leanest stage — the rig is cut from this one)
